meta.purpose: Every scripture quoted or referenced in Gideon's writings, fetched from named digital editions and verified word-for-word, banked so future work needs no repeat online confirmation.

editions.brenton: Brenton Septuagint (1851 English), eBible.org id eng-Brenton — OT only
editions.gnv: Geneva Bible 1599, eBible.org id enggnv — whole Bible
editions.kjv: King James Version 1769 standard text, eBible.org id eng-kjv2006 — whole Bible
editions.nets: NEW ENGLISH TRANSLATION OF THE SEPTUAGINT (NETS), Oxford PDF masters at ccat.sas.upenn.edu/nets/edition/ — THE SABBATH OF SCRIPTURE's OT standard (OT always NETS; LES noted where meaningfully different) NETS verse cache persisted at scripture-repository/editions/nets/nets_cache.json (Gen/Deut/Isa/Psa parsed 2026-11-07).
editions.sinaiticus: Codex Sinaiticus (Aleph 01, 4th c.) Greek readings + critical apparatus via greeknewtestament.net — the book's NT standard, codex named per quote
editions.les: Lexham English Septuagint v2 (2019, Lexham Press) — based on Swete’s Greek edition. No free public full text; rows captured only from sourced public citations (biblia.com + hermeneutics.stackexchange; thirdpeter.com posts, Aug 2026) and must be confirmed against the author’s Logos copy. Where Swete and Rahlfs Greek differ, LES follows Swete.
editions.swete_greek: Swete Septuagint Greek — theancientbible.org chapter pages (e.g. /isaiah-lxx-46/). Base text of the LES.
editions.rahlfs_greek: Rahlfs Septuagint Greek — el.wikisource.org book pages (Ησαΐας_(Rahlfs), Γένεσις_(Rahlfs)). Base text of NETS.
editions.greek_byz: Byzantine NT Greek readings via biblehub.com /text/ verse pages — used to check the author’s Greek NT annotation lines.

conventions: status: confirmed = quote matches the cited edition word-for-word; confirmed-excerpt = word-for-word but partial (ellipsis/clipped); differs-minor = same verse, few words changed; paraphrase = reworded; anchor = referenced narratively, not quoted; commentary = article's own rendering (canonical texts banked for reference).

For HALLOWED BE THY NAME: quotes cited 'LXX, Brenton' verified against Brenton's English Septuagint; quotes cited 'Geneva' against the 1599 Geneva Bible. Uncited blockquotes diagnosed against KJV (their usual voice) with GNV/Brenton banked alongside.
Psalms: the article cites Hebrew-psalm numbers (Ps 22:16); Brenton prints LXX numbers (Ps 21:17). Both recorded.
Hebrew names in the body (Moshe, Yohoshua, Yerushalayim, etc.) are the author's intentional practice - never flagged.
Ben Yachid uses JPS 1917 (Tanakh) + Geneva (NT); add JPS entries to this bank when those verses next need verification.
THE SABBATH OF SCRIPTURE (Nov 2026): OT = NETS exact; NT = ancient codex with the codex named (Sinaiticus dominant). Genesis-2 note: NETS Exodus uses 'heaven', NETS Genesis uses 'sky'.

sections.label: A Closing Word to the Body of Christ
Part One — The Old Hand — Where the Letters Were Born
sections.seeker_text: The Seeker asked: Before you show me God's Name, I have to ask a question that sits underneath all the others. Letters didn't fall from the sky. Somewhere, somebody took the first picture and made it stand for a sound — and after him the whole world learned to write. Who was he? Where did he stand? And how did Israel come by her letters? Before we open the Name, I want to meet the hand that wrote it.

nets.text: In his days Iouda will be saved, and Israel will encamp in confidence. And this is the name by which he [the Lord] will call him: “Iosedek among the prophets.” My heart was crushed; within me all my bones shook; I became like a crushed man and like a person overcome by wine, due to the Lord and due to the dignity of his glory, because due to these the land mourned, the pastures of the wilderness were dried up. And their course became evil, and their strength not so, because priest and prophet were defiled, and in my house I have seen their wickedness. Therefore let their way be to them like slipperiness in thick darkness, and they shall be tripped up and fall in it; for I will bring evil upon them in the year of their visiting. And in the prophets of Samaria I saw lawless deeds: they prophesied by the goddess Baal and led my people Israel astray. And in the prophets of Ierousalem I have seen shocking things: people committing adultery and walking in lies and strengthening the hands of evildoers so that no one turns, each from his wicked way; all have become like Sodoma to me, and its inhabitants just like Gomorra. Therefore this is what the Lord says: “Behold, I will feed them pain and will give them bitter water to drink, because from the prophets of Ierousalem defilement went out to the whole land.” Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not hear the words of the prophets, because they are rendering a vision empty. They speak from their own heart and not from the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who reject the word of the Lord, “There shall be peace for you,” and to all who walk by their own will, [to every one who walks by the error of his own heart,] they said, “No evil shall come upon you”— because who has stood in support of the Lord and seen his word? Who has given ear and obeyed? Behold, an earthquake from the Lord, and wrath goes forth as a seismic upheaval; when it gathers, it will come against the impious. And the anger of the Lord will no longer turn back until he has executed it and until he accomplished it due to the undertaking of his heart. In the last of days they will understand them. I was not sending the prophets, and they themselves kept running; I did not speak to them, and they themselves kept prophesying. And if they had stood in support of me and if they had heard my words, they would also have turned them, my people, from their evil doings. I am a god nearby, says the Lord, and not a god far off. If someone shall be hidden in secret places, is it not I that shall also see him? Do I not fill the sky and the earth? says the Lord. I have heard what the prophets are saying who prophesy lies in my name, saying, “I have dreamed a dream!” How long shall there be lies in the heart of the prophets who prophesy, when in fact they prophesy the will of their own heart, those who plan to forget my name by their dreams which they tell, each to his fellow, just as their fathers forgot my name by the goddess Baal? Let the prophet in whom there is the dream tell his dream, and let him in whom my word is to him tell my word in truth. What is the chaff to the grain? Are not my words just like fire and like an ax that cuts a rock? Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal my words each from his fellow. Behold, I am against the prophets who receive prophecies of tongue and slumber their slumber. Behold, I am against the prophets who were prophesying lying dreams, and they kept telling them, and they led my people astray by their lies and by their errors, and it was not I that sent them, and I did not command them, and they will not profit this people with profit. And if this people or a priest or a prophet asks you, “What is the issue of the Lord?” you shall then say to them, “You are the issue, and I will strike you, says the Lord.” And as for the prophet and the priest and the people who might say, “Issue of the Lord,” I will also punish that person and his household. Thus shall you say, each to his fellow and each to his brother, “What has the Lord answered?” and “What has the Lord spoken?” And “Issue of the Lord,” do not name it any more, because “the issue” will be the word belonging to the person. And what has the Lord, our God, spoken? uses.section_label: THE SABBATH OF SCRIPTURE — 4. Sinai — God Speaks the Commandment (Exodus 20 / Deuteronomy 5)
quotes: "Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill. For truly I say to you, until the heaven and the earth pass away, not one iota nor one stroke shall pass away from the Law until all things come to pass. Whoever therefore looses one of the least of these commandments and teaches men so shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens."
uses.note: Article's first half = faithful rendering of Aleph ('looses' = good literal for λυσεις/λυση; א quirks: 'κληθησετε' (apparatus: א, L), 'τω ουνων' = nomina sacra for των ουρανων). BUT the article's final clause 'but whoever does and teaches, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens' IS NOT IN CODEX SINAITICUS — Aleph omitted it (apparatus (30) OMIT ος δ αν: א, D, W; (43) OMIT μεγας κληθησεται...: א, D, W — haplography from homoeoarcton/homoeoteleuton; the clause is standard in B and the majority).

adjudication.detail: Three options: (1) drop the clause to be Sinaiticus-exact; (2) keep the clause and change the citation; (3) keep with an authorial note that Aleph skips it. NO edit without Gideon's choice.
